name: Moria
note: Fan work from Tolkien, whose work belongs to the Tolkien Estate; nothing from any book, film or game is used. The mountains, the gates' ground and the two lakes are generated by tools/make-moria.py; the gates, the halls under the mountain and everything in them are modelled in src/moria/. Positions are [lat, lon] against an origin under Zirakzigil.
attribution: Moria is fan work: generated by tools/make-moria.py and modelled in src/moria/. Tolkien's world belongs to the Tolkien Estate. No assets used.

districts._: [name, hex colour, base height, tallest, box as [lat south, lon west, lat north, lon east]]

landmarks.name: The Doors of Durin
landmarks.info: In the Walls of Moria, between two great holly-trees: the West-gate of Khazad-dum, whose Doors can be seen only under starlight and moonlight - an arch, the crown and seven stars of Durin, an anvil and hammer, two trees bearing crescent moons, and the star of the House of Feanor. Speak, friend, and enter.

landmarks.name: The Dimrill Gate
landmarks.info: The Great Gates of Khazad-dum on the east, high in the mountainside over the Dimrill Dale, with the Dimrill Stair going down from them.

landmarks.name: Durin's Tower
landmarks.info: At the top of the Endless Stair, which climbs in unbroken spiral from the lowest dungeon to the peak (press See inside to see it in the mountain): cut in the living rock of Zirakzigil, the pinnacle of Celebdil, where Gandalf and the Balrog came out onto the ice, and fought, and the tower was broken.

landmarks.name: The Dimrill Stair
landmarks.info: Steps cut in the mountainside, going down from the Great Gates into the Dimrill Dale, with a stream beside them falling in many falls to the Mirrormere.

landmarks.name: Durin's Stone
landmarks.info: A broken pillar by the Mirrormere, where Durin first looked into the lake and saw a crown of stars about his head.

landmarks.name: The Dwarrowdelf
landmarks.info: The great realm and dwarf-city of the Dwarrowdelf: a hall a kilometre long at the level of the Gates, its walls black and polished like glass, its roof carried on rows of pillars eight metres through; on its walls a gallery for every level, level above level, with doors going off into the dark.

landmarks.name: The Bridge of Khazad-dum
landmarks.info: A slender bridge of stone, without kerb or rail, across the chasm at the east end of the Second Hall in one curving spring of fifty feet; the Dwarves built it so, so that only one at a time could cross. Far below, the fire.

landmarks.name: The guard-room
landmarks.info: On the road east from the West-gate: a room off the passage, with a well in the floor by the wall, where Pippin dropped a stone and something far below began to knock.

landmarks.name: The Second Hall
landmarks.info: Loftier and longer than the Twenty-first Hall, with a double line of pillars carved like the boles of trees whose boughs hold up the roof, smooth and black; right across its floor near the feet of two of them a fissure has opened, and fire licks out of it.

landmarks.name: The Twenty-first Hall
aka: The Twenty-first Hall of the North-end
landmarks.info: On the Seventh Level, six above the Gates: a pillared hall where the Fellowship woke to grey light from shafts high in its east wall. The Chamber of Mazarbul opens off it.

landmarks.name: The Great Cistern
landmarks.info: Through the west wall of the throne-hall: pillars standing in black water in rows, causeways across it, and water falling into it out of the rock.

landmarks.name: The Hall of Durin's Throne
landmarks.info: The Third Level, up the Kings' Stair from the great hall: two rows of pillars, the throne on its dais, the crown and seven stars inlaid on the wall behind it, and down the sides of the hall the Seven Fathers of the Dwarves in stone.

landmarks.name: The Delvings
landmarks.info: The Tenth Deep, down the miners' stair from the forges: the pit of the mithril lode, a headframe over it lowering its cage, scaffolds down its sides, ore-carts going round its rim, and Moria-silver shining in the walls. The Dwarves delved too greedily and too deep.

landmarks.name: The Great Forges
landmarks.info: Through the east wall of the Mansions: two rows of hearths under their hoods and chimneys, an anvil at each, and at the end the great furnace, its channel of metal running down the hall to the moulds. Lit and ringing in Durin's day; cold in Moria.

landmarks.name: The Hall of the Mansions
landmarks.info: The Third Deep, down the Grand Stair from the great hall: a vault a hundred and fifty metres high over a city of stone houses - an avenue with a canal down it, a plaza with a fountain, streets and lanes - and on both long walls six storeys of house-fronts on terraces, with stairs climbing between them. At the west end Durin the Deathless stands sixty metres high, looking down the avenue. (This project's own invention, to sit with the book's 'dwarf-city'.)

landmarks.name: The Chamber of Mazarbul
landmarks.info: The Chamber of Records, on the Seventh Level, off the Twenty-first Hall of the North-end. Recesses in its walls with iron-bound chests in them, broken open; bones and broken weapons on the floor; and in the middle a great oblong block with a slab of white stone on it: Balin son of Fundin, Lord of Moria. A shaft of light from a window high in the east wall falls across it. A stair goes down south from its other door to the Second Hall.

landmarks.name: Kheled-zaram
landmarks.info: The long dark lake in the Dimrill Dale, in which the stars can be seen even by day; over against Durin's Stone, a crown of seven.

landmarks.name: Caradhras
landmarks.info: The cruel mountain, north of the Dwarrowdelf: the Redhorn, whose pass the Fellowship tried and was thrown back by the snow.

landmarks.name: Celebdil
landmarks.info: The Silvertine, over the halls of Khazad-dum, with Durin's Tower on its summit.

landmarks.name: Fanuidhol
landmarks.info: Cloudyhead, the southernmost of the three mountains of Moria.
